title: 01_Lowe_Coherence_Lagrangian_Formal_Test.ipynb

canonical_node.axiom: The Lowe Coherence Lagrangian (LLC) is a legitimate Lagrangian in the sense of classical mechanics, satisfying formal requirements of positive-definite mass matrix and Hamiltonian conservation.
definitions: Lagrangian: L(q, qdot, t) = chi(q,t) * (0.5 * qdot^T K qdot) - S * chi(q,t)
Mass matrix: Hessian of L with respect to qdot
derivation: Test 1: Compute mass matrix via jax.hessian of L with respect to qdot.
Check all eigenvalues positive and condition number acceptable.
Test 2: Integrate equations of motion using RK4 for N=1000 steps.
Compute Hamiltonian at each step and verify drift within numerical tolerance.
canonical_node.action: Certify the LLC as a legitimate Lagrangian based on two passed tests: positive-definite mass matrix and Hamiltonian conservation.
boundary: Does not prove physical reality or empirical validity of the LLC.
Does not establish that chi_expanded is the true chi function.
Does not address uniqueness or global validity beyond tested conditions.
test: Mass matrix eigenvalues all positive and condition number below threshold.
Hamiltonian drift consistent with machine epsilon times N for RK4.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides formal certification that the LLC satisfies Lagrangian mechanics requirements, distinguishing it from mere formulaic resemblance.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the claim that the LLC is a well-posed dynamical system with healthy kinetic structure.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this test, the LLC's legitimacy as a Lagrangian remains unverified, weakening the foundation for further derivations.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Accept as verified formal property of the LLC under specified conditions.

overstatement_risks: May be interpreted as proof of physical reality rather than mathematical consistency.
chi_expanded may not represent the full chi function, limiting generality.
Numerical tests are not mathematical proofs.
kill_conditions: If mass matrix eigenvalues are not all positive for some valid parameter range.
If Hamiltonian drift grows unboundedly with longer integration.
If chi_expanded is later shown to be an inadequate approximation.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the mass matrix positive-definiteness condition and Hamiltonian conservation as lemmas in Lean, using the specific definitions of chi_expanded and llc_lagrangian.

plain_summary: This notebook reports two numerical tests that pass, claiming the Lowe Coherence Lagrangian is a legitimate Lagrangian. The tests check positive-definiteness of the mass matrix and Hamiltonian conservation via RK4 integration. The results support the claim under the tested conditions, but they are numerical verifications, not formal proofs.
